abstract: Orthocaspases are prokaryotic homologs of metacaspases within the C14 family of cysteine proteases, yet their biochemical properties and cellular roles remain poorly understood. Here, we report the discovery and comprehensive characterization of LOca-1, a metagenome-derived orthocaspase from the Loki's Castle hydrothermal vent field. LOca-1 consists primarily of a single, conserved p20 catalytic domain and undergoes calcium-dependent activation through cleavage at a conserved arginine residue. Once activated, LOca-1 displays strict arginyl-specific proteolytic activity and strong selectivity for residues surrounding the cleavage site. The enzyme is both thermoactive and thermostable, exhibiting maximal activity at 65 {degrees}C and a melting temperature of approximately 72 {degrees}C. Structural modelling revealed conservation of the catalytic core relative to plant metacaspases despite substantial sequence divergence. To our knowledge, LOca-1 is only the second biochemically characterized orthocaspase and the first reported from a deep-sea hydrothermal vent environment. LOca-1 expands the known biochemical diversity of prokaryotic metacaspase homologs and provides insights into the properties of a minimal p20-domain orthocaspase. Together, our findings establish LOca-1 as a thermostable, calcium-activated arginyl-specific orthocaspase and provide a foundation for future studies of orthocaspase function in prokaryotes.
